what_it_is: Data security vendor with the Atlas AI security platform, from the AllTrue.ai acquisition.
identity_note: Atlas came from AllTrue.ai (announced 2026-02-03). SlashNext became Varonis Interceptor, an email and browser anti-phishing product, and is not part of Atlas.
notes: Proofpoint announced a definitive agreement to acquire Varonis on 2026-10-15 for $6.3B, expected to close in the first half of 2027. Atlas GA blog dated 2026-05-28. Agent IBAC shipped Aug 2026. Cursor integration announced 2026-07-08 and Claude Inference Hooks on 2026-08-07. Varonis for Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise and Agentforce are older data-layer products on the Data Security Platform and are separate from the Atlas gateway. The Varonis help site is gated, so most evidence comes from the Varonis blog and platform pages. Module 6: scheduled pen tests come from a SoftwareReviews page (third party) and were not found on a Varonis page. Module 2.1: platform coverage comes from the Varonis coverage pages read in the 2026-09-29 research. Module 7: the bar asks for a distinct per-agent credential, which Varonis does not document, so all three subs are partial. Gartner named Varonis a Pace Setter in the September 2026 Emerging Market Quadrant for AI Application Security.

1.reason: Atlas inventories agents, models, MCP servers across cloud, code and SaaS. Finds shadow AI via hooks and DNS.
1.evidence: Atlas inventories agents, models, tools, MCP servers, dependencies, and supporting infrastructure
1.has: Atlas AI Inventory and AI-SPM scan cloud, repos, SaaS. Hooks for Cursor, Claude Code.
1.lacks: On-prem and Kubernetes inventory not found. No browser-based shadow AI discovery found.

2.reason: Atlas covers Agentforce, AgentCore, Foundry, Copilot Studio. Finds shadow MCP, blocks bad tool calls inline.
2.evidence: teams gain visibility into both approved and shadow MCP usage
2.has: Atlas MCP discovery and tool-call blocking, Agent IBAC, coverage pages for four agent platforms.
2.lacks: Inline tool-call gating through hooks and gateway. No host sandbox found.

3.reason: Atlas AIDR alerts on prompt attacks, blocks inline, quarantines identities, and integrates with SIEM and SOAR.
3.evidence: blocks activity inline when needed, and integrates with SIEM and SOAR platforms
3.has: Atlas AIDR, inline blocking, identity quarantine, SIEM and SOAR integrations.
3.lacks: Named Atlas SIEM or ITSM connectors not documented. Blocks prompts and tool calls only.

4.reason: AI Gateway and agent hooks block PII, injection and malicious URLs in prompts and responses.
4.evidence: inspecting prompts, responses, and agent actions before they reach the model or downstream systems
4.has: Atlas AI Gateway and runtime hooks for Cursor and Claude Code. Customer-owned data plane.
4.lacks: No AI-prompt browser extension found. Toxicity and hallucination filters not documented.

5.reason: Atlas maps AI systems to EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001, with audit-ready reports.
5.evidence: continuously mapping AI systems to regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF
5.has: Atlas AI Compliance Management, audit-ready reports, lineage graphs, AI TPRM ingests vendor AIBOMs.
5.lacks: No exportable AIBOM of its own found.

6.reason: Atlas AI Pen Testing attacks live LLM endpoints, agents and MCP servers. Third-party review notes scheduled runs.
6.evidence: executing adversarial prompts and dynamic attacks against live LLM endpoints
6.has: Atlas AI Pen Testing covers injection, jailbreak, policy bypass. Results feed runtime guardrails.
6.lacks: CI/CD gating and framework-mapped findings not documented.

7.reason: Agent IBAC blocks off-intent tool calls and quarantines the agent identity. DSP classifies service accounts.
7.evidence: When an agent crosses the line, Atlas can quarantine the identity behind it and block everything that follows
7.has: Agent IBAC (shipped Aug 2026), identity quarantine, service and non-human account classification.
7.lacks: No per-agent credential or API key and OAuth grant governance documented.

8.reason: AI-SPM covers model artifacts and AI code dependencies. Databricks training data is classified, with change alerts.
8.evidence: trigger alerts when AI training data is modified
8.has: Atlas AI-SPM model artifact checks, malicious skill detection, Databricks training data classification.
8.lacks: Model file formats not named. No poisoning scans. AI code analysis not detailed.
